transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-02-11 16:00 PST
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Jonah (Redwood SE), Priya (CTO - NovaDocs), Ethan (Lead ML Eng), Sara (Product), Marcus (SRE)

Summary: quick migration/demo focused on parity mapping from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together to Redwood. Showed API differences, Console, and Optimize suggestions. Lots of discussion about latency vs cost and dedicated vs hosted options for their production workloads.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'll kick us off — quick intro, I'm Maya, I'm the AE on this account, with me is Liam and Jonah on the SE side.
[00:15] Priya: hi hi, thanks, Priya here, CTO. We're pretty keen to see how close Redwood is to what we're running on OpenAI and Together today.
[00:30] Liam: great, we'll do a parity mapping first — names, params, then demo the Redwood API and Console, and finally show Optimize suggestions for cost/perf.
[01:05] Ethan: quick context — we run a mix of OpenAI text-gen for our summarization and Together for higher-throughput conversational workloads. Token volumes spike during indexing runs, and we have latency SLOs for the chat experience. We also have strict data residency and want VPC for PII handling.
[01:35] Maya: awesome, that helps. we'll show hosted and dedicated options, and the private deployment path in case you need VPC/on-prem.
[02:10] Jonah: pulling up the parity doc — so, OpenAI model davinci-ish maps to our rdx-xxl in the catalog, and Anthropic claude-ish maps to rdx-claude-v1 equivalent. There's a spreadsheet link I put in the chat: https://redwood.app/parity/novadocs (demo link).
[02:35] Sara: perfect — does Redwood do function/tool calling like OpenAI?
[02:45] Liam: yes, we support structured outputs and function calling patterns — slightly different call shape in the SDK, but we provide drop-in RFC examples. Small differences: streaming chunk boundaries and stop token handling can differ, so we'd recommend a short compatibility shim.
[03:20] Priya: any tokenization gotchas? we do prompt-munging and sometimes rely on token counts from OpenAI.
[03:35] Liam: good question — tokenizers are similar but not identical. we include a tokenizer utility in the SDK; for safety you should run a token-histogram on your prompt set (we can help with that). also note: some Together models use different byte-pair merges so exact token counts vary slightly.
[04:05] Ethan: what about streaming? we rely on low-latency partials for the chat UI.
[04:20] Jonah: Redwood streaming is optimized for low-latency first-byte delivery. The tradeoff is batching; for high concurrency we use small micro-batches to preserve latency SLOs. there's an Optimize recommendation that suggests per-route batching profiles.
[05:00] Speaker 1: (muffled) are there SDK examples for node/react?
[05:08] Liam: yes — we have Node and Python SDKs, and example React hooks for streaming. I'll drop links after.
[05:40] Priya: security — SOC 2, SSO, KMS? we need audit logs for compliance.
[05:55] Maya: Redwood is SOC 2 compliant, supports SAML SSO, RBAC, and integrates with KMS/HSM for key management. Audit logs and request-level tracing are surfaced in Redwood Console, and for Private they can be customer-managed KMS.
[06:28] Marcus: for Private/VPC — what's the peering story and firewall requirements? we run strict egress controls.
[06:42] Jonah: for VPC we support direct peering and private endpoints; we'll provide a network checklist. For on-prem we can package the control plane and provide an air-gapped option if needed.
[07:05] Ethan: on perf — can you run a benchmark with our traces? we need to see token/sec and p99 latencies compared to OpenAI.
[07:20] Liam: absolutely. we'll provide a benchmark script and instructions to run it against hosted and dedicated nodes. Ideally you share a sample trace (anonymized) and we'll run 1:1 comparisons and show cost per 1M tokens.
[07:55] Maya: sending the parity mapping + pricing after call. Also we have a perf sheet template you can use.
[08:12] Priya: about model size and quantization — we currently use 8-bit quant on some workloads to cut cost. does Redwood support that?
[08:28] Liam: yes, Redwood supports quantized execution paths and will recommend quant profiles in Optimize based on your workload. caveat: for very latency sensitive chat we sometimes recommend mixed precision or different batching configs to avoid p99 spikes.
[09:05] Sara: how do rollouts work — can we canary new model versions?
[09:18] Jonah: yes — Redwood Console supports canary rollouts, A/B, and automatic fallback policies. You can route by percent, region, or cost tier. We also keep model versioning so you can pin a specific commit.
[09:45] Ethan: any limitations on function-calling or structured JSON generation? we sometimes need strict schema outputs.
[09:58] Liam: we have structured output tooling and schema enforcement helpers. If the model drifts, our Quality Monitoring can trigger alerts on failure rates for your eval prompts.
[10:25] Maya: (typing) dropping the parity link and a short deck: https://redwood.app/decks/migration-overview.pdf
[10:40] Priya: will we get a dedicated SLA if we go Dedicated?
[10:50] Maya: yes — Dedicated comes with commit-backed throughput, predictable latency SLOs and an SLA. For the pilot we usually start on hosted then move to dedicated once we hit committed QPS.
[11:20] Marcus: for data retention — do you store prompts or can we opt out?
[11:30] Jonah: hosted can be configured to not persist customer data; Dedicated/Private gives you full control. We support retention policies and audit logs.
[12:05] Ethan: curious about KV cache. does Redwood expose a cache or is it internal? we rely on prefix caching to reduce token costs.
[12:20] Liam: KV cache is internal to the runtime but we provide config for prefix/KV caching durations and invalidation. sometimes transcript has been transcribed as "K-V cash" in older logs, but it's K-V cache, yeah. For very large contexts we use KVM sharding and intelligent eviction.
[13:00] Priya: ok, show us a live API call mapping — how different is it to swap client code?
[13:12] Liam: demo time — I'll do a simple replace example: OpenAI completions call vs Redwood chat call. (shares code)
[13:30] Liam: OpenAI sample: client.createCompletion({model: 'gpt-4', prompt, max_tokens, temperature}) — Redwood equivalent: redwood.chat.create({model: 'rdx-4', input: prompt, max_tokens, temperature}) — almost identical, but note our stop sequences and streaming event names differ.
[14:05] Ethan: what about embeddings? we run sem-sim over docs with OpenAI embeddings; is there a drop-in?
[14:18] Jonah: yes — embeddings API is a separate endpoint but similar request/response shapes. We expose embeddings vectors and you can choose different models for cost/quality tradeoffs. There's also tokenization differences to watch for.
[15:00] Sara: show Console — cost and latency breakdown per route?
[15:10] Maya: pulling up Console — here is a per-route dashboard, shows token-level cost, latency histograms, traces and error rates; you can drill into each model and see suggested Optimize actions like reduce batch size or enable prefix caching.
[16:00] Priya: can Optimize propose quantization changes automatically?
[16:12] Liam: yes, Optimize will suggest quantization profiles and expected cost savings and the expected p99 impact. We can also run offline regression tests on your eval prompts.
[17:00] Ethan: do you support reranking workflows? we use a two-stage pipeline (retrieval -> rerank -> generate).
[17:12] Jonah: reranking is supported — you can run batch embeddings + cross-encoder style rerank on dedicated pools. We also have a rerank-specific model catalog entry.
[18:00] Priya:if we want VPC + KMS + audit logs, do we need Private right away or can we start hosted?
[18:12] Maya: you can start hosted with strict retention controls and SAML, but for full VPC/KMS integration we'd recommend Private; we can do a pilot on hosted then migrate to Private for production.
[19:00] Marcus: regulatory question — are there any compliance gaps vs what we're used to?
[19:15] Jonah: we have SOC 2, ISO options coming, and we publish our audit artifacts under NDA. For higher compliance we offer on-prem or Private with customer-managed keys.
[20:00] (discussion continues — more Q&A about networking and perf)
[30:00] Liam: dropping the benchmark repo link: https://gist.github.com/redwood/novadocs-bench (demo) — script does token-level replay and synthetic concurrency tests.
[31:10] Ethan: great, we'll run that overnight and share results.
[41:00] Maya: recap — we'll send parity mapping + pricing, Liam will share bench scripts, customer will share sample prompts and token histograms, schedule POC scoping next week.
[41:30] Priya: asking about timeline and costs for Dedicated — what's the ballpark commit?
[41:45] Maya: depends on throughput — we'll include commit tiers in the pricing doc. For many customers the pilot is 1-3 months on hosted, then a Dedicated commit after we validate perf.
[42:10] Sara: any gotchas to watch when switching quickly?
[42:25] Liam: watch tokenization and streaming behavior, and test the stop sequences. Also validate your function-calling end-to-end. We'll provide compatibility shims for a few APIs.
[50:00] Ethan: ok we want the spreadsheet and script asap.
[50:10] Maya: will do — sending now, and we'll book the POC scoping.
[51:00] Priya: thanks all, that was helpful.
[51:10] Maya: thanks everyone; ending notes — action items in chat; we'll meet again after you run the benchmark.
[52:00] (call ends)

Artifacts referenced:
- Parity mapping spreadsheet: https://redwood.app/parity/novadocs
